deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the preceding notes, not shown): C is a category with two classes of maps, cofibrations (cof) and weak equivalences (W), in roughly the style of Brown or Waldhausen. The aim is a concrete model for the localization W^{-1}C. Grothendieck works through 'fractions' of the form [f,i]: a cofibration f: x -> y' together with a weak equivalence i: y -> y' pointing backwards from y. These assemble into a category C~ with the same objects as C. There is a canonical functor C~ -> W^{-1}C sending [f,i] to i^{-1}f, and the canonical functor C -> W^{-1}C factors as C -> C~ -> W^{-1}C.

Item 6 states the difficulty. It is not clear that C~ -> W^{-1}C is faithful. Since it is the identity on objects and presumably full, faithfulness would make it an isomorphism of categories. That in turn would follow if C -> C~ inverted the maps of W, which amounts to saying that a third construction sketched earlier is valid. That construction, as far as the hand can be read, organizes the classes [f,i] in C~ into a category.

Grothendieck then draws a consequence that makes him suspicious. Put W_0 = W ∩ cof. Then C~ -> W^{-1}C would visibly factor as C~ -> W_0^{-1}C -> W^{-1}C. If C~ -> W^{-1}C were an isomorphism, W_0^{-1}C -> W^{-1}C would be an equivalence. He writes that he doubts that inverting the cofibrant weak equivalences is enough to make all weak equivalences invertible.

He therefore 'adjusts his aim' and redefines C~. Its objects are those of C. Its hom-set Hom(x,y) is pi_0 of a category Ch_0(x,y) whose objects are the diagrams x --f--> y' <--i-- y with f in cof and i in W, and whose morphisms are maps y' -> y'' compatible with f and i. In other words, he passes to connected components of the category of fraction-diagrams rather than taking equivalence classes by hand. This is the standard 'calculus of fractions up to homotopy' description of Hom in a homotopy category. Its modern form is due to Dwyer–Kan (1980): with a homotopy calculus of fractions, the hammock localization is the nerve of the category of zigzags. For cofibration categories it appears in Brown (1973), Rădulescu-Banu (2006) and Cisinski ('Catégories dérivables', 2010). The page breaks off at the definition.
errors: The doubt that inverting W_0 = W ∩ cof suffices is unfounded in the standard settings. In a Brown/Waldhausen cofibration category with factorizations, Ken Brown's factorization lemma writes every weak equivalence between cofibrant objects as a trivial cofibration followed by a retraction of a trivial cofibration. Hence W_0^{-1}C -> W^{-1}C is an equivalence on cofibrant objects (all objects, in Waldhausen's setting). Whether the doubt is justified depends on axioms of his C that this page does not state, e.g. the absence of factorizations.
'fidèle (i.e. = un iso)' tacitly assumes that C~ -> W^{-1}C is already full and bijective on objects. That is plausible here but not argued on this page.

ideas.what: Represent morphisms of W^{-1}C by fractions x -> y' <- y (cofibration followed by an inverted weak equivalence) and ask when this is faithful.
ideas.modern_name: right calculus of fractions in a cofibration category
ideas.where_published: possibly echoed in Pursuing Stacks / Les Dérivateurs discussions of localizers

ideas.what: Comparison W_0^{-1}C -> W^{-1}C with W_0 = trivial cofibrations: is localizing at trivial cofibrations enough?
ideas.modern_name: Ken Brown's lemma / localization at trivial cofibrations

ideas.what: Hom(x,y) := pi_0 of the category Ch_0(x,y) of zigzags x -cof-> y' <-W- y.
ideas.modern_name: homotopy calculus of fractions; pi_0 of the 2-arrow hammock category

deep.surprise_reason: Routine working through of the fraction description of a homotopy category, a few years after Brown and Dwyer–Kan. The one non-standard remark, doubting that trivial cofibrations suffice, is actually refuted by Ken Brown's lemma in standard settings.
transcription_corrections: The parenthetical after 'fidèle' is mostly illegible. It probably says '(ce qui impliquerait que c'est un iso[morphisme] = des deux équivalences de catégories)'; the '$\mathcal{H}$ variant' reading is doubtful.
'par un ensemble [?] de [f,i]' is uncertain. It may read 'par un calcul de [f,i]' or similar; the general sense is a construction on the classes [f,i] in C~.
Under the second 'C~ -> W_0^{-1}C -> W^{-1}C' there is an isomorphism sign (≀) under C~ with W^{-1}C written below. Grothendieck is recording the hypothetical identification C~ ≅ W^{-1}C.
